title: Keeping Up with Science: Ordinary WiFi Can Identify You (A2)

elements.content: Welcome to Keeping Up with Science. Review the research context and metadata below:

Session Overview:
• Duration: 60 minutes
• Languages: 🇬🇧 English
• Level: Elementary (A2)
• Theme: WiFi Technology & Smart Homes

What is your initial reaction when reading about this scientific study?
How might this discovery change how we understand daily health or technology?
Master the core scientific vocabulary and collocations for this topic (10 items):

items.definition: a wireless way to connect computers and phones to the internet.
items.example: Our home WiFi works in every room.

items.definition: waves that carry information through the air.
items.example: The WiFi signal gets weak near the balcony.

items.definition: a device that sends internet signals to your devices.
items.example: Restart the router if the internet stops working.

items.definition: a vertical side of a room.
items.example: WiFi signals can pass through wooden walls.
A phone can identify your face to unlock.

items.definition: to move on foot at a regular pace.
items.example: Each person has a unique way they walk.

items.definition: something that is kept hidden from others.
items.example: Keep your personal WiFi password secret.

items.definition: having or showing intelligence or computer technology.
items.example: Smart homes use WiFi to turn on lights.

items.definition: not in danger or likely to be hurt.
items.example: We want our personal data to be safe.

items.definition: to examine something to see if it works.
items.example: Scientists tested the new WiFi system in an office.

elements.title: Grammar Explanation (Elementary (A2))
elements.content:
Use can + base verb to talk about modern technological capabilities (e.g., Ordinary WiFi can identify people through walls).
🧩 Interactive Word Bank:
Tap a word chip below, then tap any empty bracket [_____] to place it!
can
identify
see
detect
base verb
📝 Task 1 : Part A: Rule Formulation:
Complete the rule: Express present possibility with 'can' + _____ without 'to'.
📝 Task 1 : Part B: Structured Practice:
Ordinary WiFi _____ people by how they walk.
Radio signals _____ through thin walls.
Smart routers _____ movement in the living room.

🗣️ Task 2 : Interactive Speaking:
Tell your partner two things modern smartphones can do.
A comparative reflection on our habits and self-perceptions.
Analyze the core scientific findings and discuss the personal prompts in pairs:

prompts: Do you use wireless WiFi or a cable connection at home?
How strong is the internet signal in your bedroom or kitchen?
Where is your home internet router placed?
Can WiFi waves pass through a thick concrete wall easily?
How can smart technology identify a person by their movement patterns?
How far do you walk every day during your normal routine?
Why should you keep your private passwords and PIN codes a secret?
What smart devices do you have in your house?
Is it safe to connect to public free WiFi networks in cafes?
How do engineers test new internet technologies before releasing them?
